subject: Request: pilot window extension for onboarding — microservice regression
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nimbustech.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 15:14:02 -0700
Subject: Pilot blocked by microservice regression — asking for extension and sandbox credits

Hi Chloe,

Quick note from our side — we hit an unexpected regression in our ingress microservice while wiring up the Redwood connector. The error surfaces during the handshake: payloads are being dropped intermittently and the health check returns 500 for a specific code path. Our SREs traced it to a recent change in our queueing layer; the fix is non-trivial because it impacts downstream idempotency logic.

This means our pilot demo and the security/infra run-throughs scheduled next week will likely be delayed by at least 2–3 weeks. We really want to keep moving with Redwood (product and perf look great), but we’re going to need extra runway to get past this technical blocker.

Could Redwood grant a 3-week trial extension and a sandbox credit top-up (approx 50k tokens) so we can finish integration and complete the SOC/ops checklist? I attached the error log and a screenshot of the failing health check.

Appreciate any help you can offer — if useful I can hop on a quick screenshare and walk your onboarding engineer through the specific stack traces.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Lead Engineer, Nimbus Labs
samir.patel@nimbustech.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments:
- error_log.txt (text)
- screenshot-500.png (image)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nimbustech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 17:05:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot blocked by microservice regression — asking for extension and sandbox credits

Hi Samir — thanks for the detail and for sending the logs. Sorry to hear you ran into this right before the demo window.

Immediate plan: I’ve looped in Karthik (onboarding engineering) so we can triage the logs quickly. Two quick asks to help us move faster:
- Can you confirm whether the failing path is reproducible on a smaller dataset (so our SE can reproduce without full production traffic)?
- If there’s a consolidated stack trace or the git commit that introduced the queueing change, please paste that in the thread.

From a commercial perspective I’m prepared to request a one-time courtesy extension while you stabilize. Can you confirm the desired extension period (you mentioned 2–3 weeks — I’ll request 21 days) and that 50k tokens is the right ballpark for sandbox usage?

If approved we’ll:
- Add a 21-day trial extension to your pilot, effective from your existing trial end date.
- Provision a 50k-token sandbox top-up to the account.

I’ll escalate for manager sign-off now. If you’re able to screenshare on Monday morning that would help us triage faster — Karthik, would you be available for a short session Monday 09:30 PT?

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
(650) 555-0114

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nimbustech.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 10:22:06 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot blocked by microservice regression — asking for extension and sandbox credits

Hi Samir / Chloe — I reviewed the attached log and the failure pattern looks like the queueing change is causing duplicate deliveries on retry, which can surface as 500s in our connector when idempotency headers are absent. We should be able to work around this in two ways:

1) Quick mitigation (recommended): patch the connector to tolerate duplicate deliveries (10–15m change) + add a short-lived header mapper.
2) Longer term: we advise fixing the upstream idempotency in your queueing layer.

Commercially I’m happy to green-light the extension Chloe proposed as a one-time exception: 21 days added to the pilot and a 50k-token sandbox top-up. Conditions:
- We’ll provision the tokens immediately.
- If the regression is not resolved within 10 business days we’ll schedule a dedicated troubleshooting session with one of our Senior SEs (up to 4 hours) to pair with your team.

I’ve attached the approval stub for records. Chloe — please push the 21-day change and the sandbox credit to Nimbus Labs (DEAL-4872). Samir — can you confirm Monday 09:30 PT for a troubleshooting screenshare so we can try the quick mitigation first?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Onboarding Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
